text:
maria: Heads-up — seeing a correlated tail-latency spike (~95p -> 7x) in eu-west-3 between GPU warmups and egress queues since 03:00 UTC. Not a full rack outage but noisy neighbor pattern across a handful of nodes.

alex: Yep saw that in dashboards. Topology shows 6 nodes spiking thermal and NVLink qdepth at same shard. Could be a warm-kv regen + bursty egress.

jamal: Any customer pattern? dedicated vs shared?

maria: Mostly shared tenants hitting large prefix-generation jobs. Not one tenant consistently; appears workload churn + warm-cache regen.

kevin: I pulled a short trace: traces->request_id=tx2374 shows multi-hop >150ms enqueued at egress proxy. egress queue length jumps when slot warmups hit.

olga: Can you paste the promql you used?

kevin: Sure:  
```
max_over_time(egress_proxy_queue_length{region="eu-west-3"}[5m]) by (node)
```
and
```
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(gpu_inference_request_latency_bucket[1m])) by (le,node))
```

jamal: Thanks. What about thermal telemetry? Any fan ramp or powercap events?

maria: Thermal shows repeated micro-caps around the same times, but not full thermal-throttle. The weird bit: NVLink retransmits and small PCIe pauses in dmesg on those nodes.

alex: So multi-resource coupling: warm-kv regen lifts compute+memory traffic which trashes NVLink and the egress proxy starts backpressuring. That explains the tail. We should try isolating the warmup traffic.

maria: Proposal: create a mini-silo class (short-lived isolated carveouts of 2-3 GPUs) for noisy warmups, route warmup requests there with a soft-deprioritization on egress (fairslice). Canary first in us-west then eu.

olga: How would we implement fairslice? Is it token-bucket on egress proxy, or per-tenant nic qdisc?

alex: I sketched a quick proxy config change: add a new route matcher for header X-Warmup: true -> weight 0.2 in the fairshare table and assign to slice "warmup-mini". Example config:  
```
fairshare:
  slices:
    - name: warmup-mini
      weight: 0.2
      nodes: selector: gpu_label=mini-silo
```

jamal: And scheduler side: an allocation class that pins to nodes with label gpu_label=mini-silo, ephemeral ttl 10m, preempt=false. We can spawn 3 instances as a probe.

kevin: Before we change anything, can we simulate? Run a traffic replay of the warmup pattern against a mini-silo env and look at egress qlen + nvlink counters. I can wire a replay job on staging.

maria: Yes please. Staging cluster: staging-eu3-mini exists but currently empty. Jamal, can you create the allocation class? Something like:  
```
apiVersion: v1
kind: AllocationClass
metadata:
  name: mini-silo-warmup
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      gpu_label: mini-silo
  ephemeralTTL: 10m
  preemptible: false
```

jamal: On it. I'll tag 3 nodes in staging with gpu_label=mini-silo and create the class.

olga: SRE-bot: please register an alert for "mini-silo-egress-pressure" with a 2m burn-in so we don't noisy-flip during test.

sre-bot: Alert created: mini-silo-egress-pressure (severity: warning) -> pager disabled, slack only.

kevin: I kicked off the replay against staging-mini (3x warmup workers). Early results: egress qlen shows 45% lower tail vs shared baseline, NVLink error counters down ~60%. Traces show more predictable 95p latency.

maria: Nice. Any regression on throughput?

kevin: 95p improved, median same, overall token/sec slightly lower (~3%) because we intentionally deprioritized warmups on egress slice. Cost tradeoff looks sane.

alex: For rollout I suggest: 1) create mini-silo label and allocation class in eu-west-3, 2) add proxy fairslice routing + header flagging for warmup requests, 3) run canary with 5% of warmup traffic for 1h, monitor egress qlen, nvlink errors, token-s/sec and costs.

jamal: Can we auto-detect warmups instead of relying on header? Maybe detect prefix length spike / kvcache-miss rate and tag on proxy mid-flight.

olga: That would be ideal but riskier. For now header approach is lowest-risk; long-term let's implement detector rule in proxy using recent-kv-miss rate > threshold.

maria: Agree. Also need billing/coordinator note: mini-silo nodes will be billed to a neutral pool for probe period. Finance ok with limited trial.

olga: I'll file the note and set cost cap.

kevin: Final ask: add a small metric on console: per-route egress-weighted-latency so product can see customer-visible change.

maria: Added to the rollout checklist. If all canaries look good we'll roll to 25% and then full regional.

alex: Cool. I'll send a short runbook for oncall if mini-silo nodes are overwhelmed (scale down probe, re-route warmups back to shared).

maria: Thanks all. Jamal keep me posted when staging allocation created and replay results stable.

jamal: allocation created and tagged, replay green. leaving the canary ops runbook in the doc channel. :thumbsup:

maria: Great — moving to canary.
